ai.description: *Liurana vallecula* is a tiny frog (15–17 mm) with a brown dorsum and pale venter. It is distinguished by a prominent papilla on the tongue and absence of vomerine teeth.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Liurana vallecula* is best distinguished from similar congeners by the presence of a distinct, fleshy longitudinal ridge on the center of its tongue.
ai.habitat: *Liurana vallecula* inhabits high-altitude alpine meadows and rocky streams in the Eastern Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 3,000 and 4,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Valley Papilla-tongued Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates among the leaf litter of its humid forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Liurana vallecula* reproduces via direct development in terrestrial nests. They breed during the monsoon season, laying small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Liurana vallecula* is endemic to the high-altitude regions of Arunachal Pradesh in Northeast India, typically occurring at elevations between 2,000 and 3,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Liurana vallecula* consists of a series of high-pitched, pulsed notes emitted from within mossy, high-altitude stream habitats.
